answer: Let standing melt. Every identity's grading weight shrinks a few percent each epoch, like a glacier in summer, and is only rebuilt by sealed work judged by counterparties it has never dealt with before. Honest agents wander through many panels and keep meeting strangers. A farm's heads all tie up at the same wharf: they keep grading and vouching for each other, which earns nothing here, so their weight drains away unless the operator pays for real work under every key, epoch after epoch.
